name: Crawler dozer
subtitle: 65-70 t class, semi-U blade and ripper -- D375A / D10 / BD355 family
summary: The machine that makes the mine work. Dozers build and dress benches, cut ramps, clean up around the shovel, push the dump edge, and build the berms that stop trucks going over it. They also rip soft rock and coal that does not need blasting.
specs: approx. 65-70 t with blade and ripper
semi-U, approx. 18 m3, approx. 5 m wide x 2.2 m high
single shank, penetration up to approx. 1.5 m
approx. 8 m with blade and ripper
safety: Dump-edge work: push from a safe distance with a berm in front, never drive to the crest to look over it.
Seat belt always -- the ROPS only protects a belted operator.
Lower blade and ripper to the ground whenever the dozer is parked or anyone works on it.
Keep 2-3 machine lengths clear of the shovel and trucks, and get the shovel operator's acknowledgement before entering its swing.
ar_tips: Stand in front of the blade: at 2.2 m high it is taller than you, and the operator cannot see you from the seat.
Walk to the back to see the ripper tip -- the shank goes into the ground under where you would be standing.

parts.label: Crawler tracks
parts.note: 610 mm single-grouser shoes. Ground pressure is about 1.4 kg/cm2, which is why a 70 t dozer can work a wet dump edge a truck could never reach. Undercarriage is roughly half a dozer's lifetime repair bill -- avoid needless high-speed reverse and spinning on rock.

parts.label: Sprocket, idler & rollers
parts.note: Final drive and sprocket at the rear, recoil spring and idler at the front. Check track sag every shift: too tight and the bushings wear fast, too loose and the track can come off on a side slope.

parts.label: Main frame & fenders
parts.note: Box-section frame carrying the engine, transmission and the track-frame pivot shaft. The fenders double as walkways -- three points of contact getting on and off.

parts.label: Engine compartment
parts.note: Diesel of about 450 kW driving a torque converter and powershift transmission. The torque converter lets the operator load the blade until the tracks are about to slip, without stalling the engine.

parts.label: Radiator & front guard
parts.note: Heavy guard over the radiator: the blade throws rock back towards the machine. A blocked core is the usual cause of overheating on a dusty bench -- blow it out daily.

parts.label: Exhaust & air precleaner
parts.note: Intake is taken high and through a cyclone precleaner, away from the dust the blade raises.

parts.label: Cab with ROPS / FOPS
parts.note: Roll-Over and Falling-Object Protective Structure. It only works if the operator is wearing the seat belt -- dozers work on slopes and dump edges, and roll-overs kill unbelted operators.

parts.label: Cab glazing
parts.note: The operator watches the blade corners and the ripper tip, both through glass. Keep it clean; on a dump edge the view of the crest is the whole job.

parts.label: Fuel tank
parts.note: Behind the cab, protected by the ripper frame. Refuel with the blade and ripper grounded and the engine off.

parts.label: Handrails & steps
parts.note: Access is up the left side over the track. Never use the tracks or the blade lift cylinders as a step.

parts.label: Semi-U blade (approx. 18 m3)
parts.note: Straight centre with angled wings, so it carries a big load without spilling at the ends, yet still cuts. Productive pushing distance is short -- beyond about 60-90 m a dozer loses most of its load and a loader and truck are cheaper.

parts.label: Cutting edge & end bits
parts.note: Bolt-on, reversible and replaceable. Run it down to the bolt holes and you are wearing out the moldboard itself.

parts.label: Push arms
parts.note: Transfer the whole tractive effort of the tracks into the blade. They pivot on trunnions on the track frames, so the blade rises and falls in an arc.

parts.label: Lift & tilt cylinders
parts.note: Two lift cylinders raise and lower the blade, a tilt cylinder drops one corner to cut a ditch or a crossfall. Never work under a raised blade: lower it to the ground.

parts.label: Ripper frame
parts.note: Parallelogram linkage that keeps the shank at a constant angle as it goes down. Ripping lets a dozer loosen soft rock and coal so it can be pushed or loaded with no blasting.

parts.label: Ripper shank & tip
parts.note: Single shank, penetration up to about 1.5 m. Rip in the direction the trucks or dozer will push, and lift out before turning -- turning with the shank in the ground breaks it.

parts.label: Ripper cylinders
parts.note: Lift and tip cylinders. The tip cylinder rocks the shank to pry rock loose as the dozer moves forward.

parts.label: 1.8 m person (for scale)
parts.note: A person in PPE, 1.8 m tall, standing clear of the machine. Use the scale toggle to hide them. In real AR at 1:1 you can simply walk up to the machine yourself.
